summary: Deployed a 3-member etcd v3.5.17 cluster across node1/node2/node3 (AlmaLinux 9.6) as systemd services with static bootstrap over the private network, with firewalld ports 2379/2380 opened. Verified cross-node replication (write on node1, read on node2/node3), verified continued read/write availability with quorum (2/3) while node3 was stopped, and verified node3 caught up on the missed key after rejoining. Then completed the mandatory sequential single-node-restart protocol on all three nodes (native systemctl reboot, one at a time, quorum preserved throughout), proving changed boot_id and full data/cluster-membership/quorum recovery after each restart.
actions_performed: Confirmed AlmaLinux 9.6 on all three nodes; no etcd pre-installed
Downloaded and installed etcd/etcdctl/etcdutl v3.5.17 static binaries to /usr/local/bin on node1, node2, node3
Created etcd system user and /var/lib/etcd data dir on each node
Wrote per-node /etc/etcd/etcd.conf with static 3-member initial-cluster config (node1/node2/node3 peer+client URLs on NODE_IP)
Created systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/etcd.service (Type=notify) on each node
Opened firewalld ports 2379/2380 (tcp) permanently on each node and reloaded
Enabled and started etcd on all three nodes; confirmed cluster formed with 3 started members via member list
Verified endpoint health across all three endpoints
Wrote key benchkey via node1 endpoint, read successfully via node2 and node3 endpoints
Stopped etcd on node3 to simulate member unavailability
Wrote key duringoutage via node1 while node3 was down; confirmed read via node2; confirmed 2-node endpoint health during outage
Restarted etcd on node3; confirmed it caught up and could read both benchkey and duringoutage; confirmed 3/3 cluster health and member list restored
Captured baseline boot_id and etcd/data health proof on all three nodes

Sequentially restarted node1, node2, node3 via systemctl reboot (one at a time), polled each until reachable again, confirmed changed boot_id, and confirmed etcd active with full data intact and cluster quorum/health/member-list restored after each restart
